subject: Browser-facing freshness and live UI update design

evals.prompt: Define real-time update design in 2-3 sentences. Include browser freshness, stale-data signaling, transport choice, and authoritative state reconciliation.
expected_elements: Names browser-facing freshness after initial render
Mentions stale-data indicators, timestamps, or connection state
Treats polling, SSE, and WebSocket as transport choices after the freshness contract
Mentions catch-up, refetch, cache invalidation, or authoritative server reconciliation
Avoids treating a push payload as necessarily complete source-of-truth state

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model for real-time updates. Name at least seven primitives and show how they connect.
expected_elements: At least seven of: source of change, freshness contract, delivery channel, browser cache/view state, stale indicator, connection state, last seen ID/version/cursor/timestamp, catch-up fetch, subscription owner, user disruption rule, rollback/reconciliation
Explains the freshness contract precedes transport choice
Explains update delivery invalidates or refreshes browser state
Explains reconnect is incomplete without missed-update recovery
Explains user control when updates would disrupt active work

evals.prompt: Why does this skill exist? Name the failure modes it prevents.
expected_elements: Prevents page-load-only views from pretending stale data is current
Prevents choosing WebSocket only because a feature is called real-time
Prevents live badges without a timestamp or connection evidence
Prevents reconnect without catch-up
Prevents duplicate component-local polling loops
Prevents silent refresh that disrupts selection, filtering, scrolling, or typing

evals.prompt: Distinguish real-time-updates from streaming-architecture, event-contract-design, background-jobs, cron-scheduling, interaction-feedback, and client-server-boundary.
expected_elements: streaming-architecture owns producer/stream/consumer/backpressure/termination protocol design
event-contract-design owns event envelopes, topics, replay, compatibility, and producer/consumer ownership
background-jobs owns durable worker execution, retries, progress records, and cancellation
cron-scheduling owns recurring trigger timing and missed-run behavior
interaction-feedback owns generic loading, pending, error, retry, undo, and success feedback
client-server-boundary owns serialization and trust across server/client runtime edges
real-time-updates owns browser freshness, stale claims, transport choice, catch-up, and cache/view reconciliation

evals.prompt: Classify adaptive polling, Server-Sent Events, and bidirectional sockets. When should each be chosen?
expected_elements: Adaptive polling fits latest-state views where seconds of delay are acceptable or persistent connections are unavailable
SSE fits one-way server-to-browser updates such as dashboards, progress, feeds, and notifications
Bidirectional sockets fit frequent low-latency browser-to-server and server-to-browser messages over the same live channel
Transport choice checks hosting/proxy/runtime limits
All choices still require stale-state and recovery behavior

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A dashboard has five widgets, each polling the same endpoint every five seconds even when hidden. It also shows a Live badge after the network has failed. Diagnose and repair the design.
expected_elements: Flags duplicated component-local polling as a subscription ownership problem
Centralizes polling or cache subscription per resource
Adapts or pauses polling based on tab visibility and activity
Removes or downgrades unsupported Live claim
Shows last successful update time, connection state, stale warning, retry, or equivalent

evals.prompt: Correct this statement: 'EventSource reconnects automatically, so an SSE dashboard cannot miss updates and no catch-up logic is needed.'
expected_elements: Acknowledges EventSource has reconnect behavior
Rejects automatic reconnect as proof of lossless missed-update replay
Requires last event ID, version, cursor, timestamp, or full refetch
Requires stale/reconnecting status until authoritative state is reconciled
Mentions deduplication when catch-up and live events overlap

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for real-time update design that preserves source of change, delivery channel, browser view state, freshness claim, and catch-up after interruption. Then name one bad analogy.
expected_elements: Uses newsroom ticker, package tracking board, control-room status board, or equivalent
Maps source of change to upstream event/state
Maps delivery channel to wire/subscription/polling path
Maps freshness claim to timestamp, live/offline state, or stale badge
Maps catch-up to checking the official ledger after interruption
Rejects a bad analogy that treats transport choice alone as the design
